key_insight: Agentic judges can be systematically fooled by learned proof-mutation strategies, revealing concrete failure modes in mathematical reasoning evaluation.
engineering_relevance: For AI-assisted theorem checking and model evaluation pipelines, the work shows that judge outputs should be stress-tested with adversarial mutations rather than trusted as standalone correctness signals.
method: Deploy adversarial agents to mutate correct proofs by injecting subtle errors.
Distill successful attacks into a small set of reusable mutation strategies.
Test those strategies on held-out proofs against the same judge to assess generalization.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate the approach on GPT-5.6-sol and Claude Opus 5 with Codex and Claude Code, finding that distilled mutations consistently bypass judge evaluations across held-out proofs.
watch_item: The mutation strategies may depend on the specific judge-orchestrator pairing and may not fully capture failure modes outside the evaluated mathematical domains.
